text: dsh-refkeeper 是 DSH 网页端的参考文献插件，在输入区提供捕获面板，并注册引用捕获、核验、保存、导出工具及 /refs 命令。它从当前或历史对话提取书目，查询学术注册源核对标题、年份和首位作者；通过核验的条目保存到工作区，其他条目隔离。用户可管理文献并导出 BibTeX 或 RIS，适合整理研究对话中的引用，无需 API 密钥。

dsh-refkeeper manages references in DSH. Its composer panel and /refs command capture citations, check titles, years and authors against scholarly registries, then store verified entries and quarantine others. Users can manage references and export BibTeX or RIS without an API key.

dsh-refkeeper 的功能「capture」：捕获当前轮、最近若干轮或整段对话中的 DOI、arXiv 编号及格式化书目条目。 通过 /refs 命令或输入区面板触发，处理当前会话的书目数据。
dsh-refkeeper 的功能「verify」：查询多个学术注册源并对照标题、年份和首位作者，返回核验状态。 通过 /refs 命令或输入区面板触发，处理当前会话的书目数据。
dsh-refkeeper 的功能「store」：将核验通过的参考文献写入工作区文献库，未确认条目单独隔离。 通过 /refs 命令或输入区面板触发，处理当前会话的书目数据。
dsh-refkeeper 的功能「export」：把文献库或最近捕获的条目渲染并导出为 BibTeX 或 RIS。 通过 /refs 命令或输入区面板触发，处理当前会话的书目数据。
dsh-refkeeper 的功能「panel」：在会话输入区打开面板，选择捕获范围、编辑条目并选择导出格式。 通过 /refs 命令或输入区面板触发，处理当前会话的书目数据。
dsh-refkeeper 核验与补全引用时会向 Crossref、OpenAlex、arXiv 和 DataCite 发起查询请求，查询中包含用户提供的 DOI、标题或其他书目信息。

dsh-refkeeper README · dsh-refkeeper：**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-refkeeper) [](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin. It reads a conversation, collects the papers that conversation cited, checks each paper against Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv and DataCite, and exports the confirmed entries as BibTeX or RIS. Papers that fail the check go into a separate quarantine file instead of the library.

dsh-refkeeper README · dsh-refkeeper：If this plugin saves you time, a star on GitHub helps other people find it. If you hit a bug or want a feature, open an issue — Chinese or English, either is fine. I read all of them and add the useful ones to the roadmap.

dsh-refkeeper README · What it does：- **Collects citations.** Scope can be one turn, the last N turns, or the whole session. It recognises DOIs, arXiv ids, ISBNs and report numbers, and also reference lines written in APA, GB/T 7714 or IEEE style.
- **Checks them against registries.** An entry is accepted only if the title matches, the year is within one year, the first author matches, and at least one registry returned a record.
- **Writes annotations.** After a capture, the model already running the session writes four short fields per entry: a summary, why the paper is relevant here, a supporting quote, and caveats. A quote that does not appear in the conversation is dropped.
- **Exports.** BibTeX, RIS, or both. The export can cover the last capture, the entries you ticked, or the whole library.

dsh-refkeeper README · One button in the composer：The interface gains exactly one thing: an item in the composer's tool row, standing next to the work-mode and model pickers. It reads `❝ Refs` (Chinese UI: `❝ 引用`). There is no sidebar, no toolbar and no floating widget — press it and the capture panel opens above the composer, close it and the row is back to what it was.

dsh-refkeeper README · Why not just copy the citations by hand：For three papers, copy by hand. Past that it is slow and easy to get wrong: one DOI sits in a tool result, an APA line sits in a summary, another paper is only mentioned by name two turns earlier.

Asking the model for a `.bib` file is faster, but models make up page ranges, DOIs and author order, and the mistake is usually found at submission time.
section: Why not just copy the citations by hand

text:
dsh-refkeeper README · Why not just copy the citations by hand：| | Copy by hand | Ask a model for a `.bib` | This plugin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source of the list | your reading | the model's memory | parsed from the conversation you select |
| Metadata checked | no | no | Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv, DataCite |
| What happens to a paper that cannot be confirmed | n/a | kept | moved to `refs/quarantine.json`, excluded from export |
| Invented pages, DOIs, authors | n/a | possible | fields come from registry records; unsupported fields stay empty |
| Why the paper is there | lost | lost | annotation plus a verbatim quote |
| Same export twice | n/a | unlikely | identical bytes; entries sorted, citekeys stable |
| Citations you never used | not included | included | excluded by default: tool output is not treated as a citation |

dsh-refkeeper README · Install：In DSH open **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `dsh-refkeeper`. The package is published on npm, so this is one step and runs no build: the tarball ships the built `lib/`. Enable it for the current profile, then reload.

To track the repository instead of the published version, paste the Git address `https://github.com/ymwang92/dsh-refkeeper` into the same dialog. The repository commits `lib/` too, so that route needs no build either.

dsh-refkeeper README · Use：1. Open a conversation that cited papers and open the capture panel above the composer.
2. Choose the scope, then **Capture & save**.
3. The panel lists what was saved and what went to the ⚠ quarantine. Untick any entry you do not want.
4. Choose BibTeX and/or RIS, then **Export this capture**.

The same steps as commands:

```text
/refs capture --scope=all --save
/refs export --format=both
```

dsh-refkeeper README · Use：Files are written to `refs/` inside the session's workspace. To export into a specific folder, paste its path in the panel once; it is remembered in `refs/settings.json`. Folders outside the session workspace are refused, because the host only allows writes inside it.

dsh-refkeeper README · What the output looks like：`refs/annotated.md` is the reading copy:

text:
dsh-refkeeper README · How a paper is accepted or rejected：```text
conversation text
   │  identifiers: DOI, arXiv id, ISBN, report number
   │  reference lines: APA, GB/T 7714, IEEE
   ▼

`unverified` is a third status, used when the registries could not be reached. The entry stays in the library and can be retried later; a network failure is not evidence that a citation is wrong. `quarantined` means the registries answered and disagreed.
section: How a paper is accepted or rejected

text: dsh-refkeeper README · Annotations：Four fields: `summary`, `relevance`, `evidence`, `caveats`. They are written after a capture by the profile's default model, from the conversation lines that mention the paper. A prompt rule and a parser filter both reject sentences that describe the absence of information ("the excerpt does not mention this work"); such a field is stored as empty and omitted from the export, so BibTeX gets no empty `note` and RIS gets no empty `N1`.

dsh-refkeeper README · Annotations：The model call happens once per capture, with a 60 second cap, and covers at most 12 entries. Entries beyond that budget, or captures without a reachable model, keep their bibliographic fields and the capture result says why annotations were skipped. The `ref_save` tool still accepts annotations you write yourself, and existing user annotations are never overwritten.

dsh-refkeeper README · Chinese references：GB/T 7714 reference lines are parsed along with APA and IEEE. Chinese titles are matched against registry records by character bigrams (Dice ≥ 0.90) rather than word tokens, because romanised records otherwise never match. `language` is carried into both export formats.

Registry coverage for Chinese journals is thin: CNKI, Wanfang and CQVIP links are only used to extract identifiers, not queried as registries. Expect more manual correction there than for a paper with an English DOI.

dsh-refkeeper README · The panel：| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | this turn, the last N turns, or the whole session |
| Capture & save | captures, verifies, annotates and stores; the result lists what was saved and what went to the quarantine |
| Row checkbox | which entries the next export includes; saved rows are ticked, ⚠ rows are not |
| Expand a row | shows the stored fields; edits are saved per entry |
| Format | BibTeX, RIS, or both |
| Folder | export destination; empty means `refs/exports/` |
| Export this capture | writes the ticked entries |
| Export all references | writes the whole library |

dsh-refkeeper README · Commands：| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Preview what the conversation cites | `/refs capture --scope=all --dry-run` |
| Capture and store | `/refs capture --scope=lastN --turns=5 --save` |
| Check one reference | `/refs verify --doi=10.1002/joc.1688` |
| Read the library | `/refs list [--quarantine]` |
| Fill in missing volume, pages, publisher | `/refs enrich [--quarantine]` |
| Promote verified quarantine entries | `/refs promote [--ids=<payload>]` or `/refs promote --manual --reason=<text>` |
| Edit one field | `/refs edit --id=<id> --payload=<base64url(json)>` |
| Remove entries | `/refs remove <id\|doi\|arxiv>...` or `/refs remove --all --yes` |
| Export | `/refs export [--format=bibtex\|ris\|both] [--all] [--ids=...] [--out=path]` |
| Set the export folder | `/refs dir --set=<base64url(path)>` or `/refs dir --clear` |

dsh-refkeeper README · Commands：<details>
<summary>Full command reference</summary>

```text
/refs                                                     capture readiness
/refs capture [--scope=turn|lastN|all] [--turns=N] [--save] [--dry-run] [--include-tools]
/refs verify --doi=... | --arxiv=... | --title=... [--json]
/refs save --json='{...}'

dsh-refkeeper README · Commands：`/refs promote` re-verifies quarantine entries against live registries and moves only `verified` results. `--ids` narrows it to the rows you ticked in the panel, which is what the two buttons on a quarantined row send: "Re-verify" runs the checks, "Store as manual" moves the row with a recorded `manual` status and a reason. A promoted entry that already exists in the library replaces that row instead of leaving the old record behind.

dsh-refkeeper README · Commands：Without `--save`, `/refs capture` only previews candidates. Export defaults to the
last saved capture; `--all` exports the library instead. Long identifiers are
passed base64url-encoded because real ids contain spaces, `<>`, `;` and parentheses.

dsh-refkeeper README · Commands：The same work is stored once even if both tables knew about it: a reference that
quarantined first and was captured successfully later is merged by identity
(DOI, arXiv id, ISBN or title + year), and `remove` / `edit` apply to both
tables so the leftover copy cannot resurface in an `--include-quarantine`
export.

</details>

dsh-refkeeper README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ref_capture` | collect candidate references from the conversation |
| `ref_verify` | check one identifier or title against the registries |
| `ref_save` | store a reference with annotations you supply |
| `ref_export` | write BibTeX/RIS for a batch, a selection, or the library |
| `ref_ping` | report which host services and registries are reachable |

dsh-refkeeper README · Files：```text
refs/refs.json          accepted references, with their annotations
refs/quarantine.json    ⚠ entries that failed the check
refs/last-capture.json  result of the last capture; default export scope
refs/settings.json      remembered export folder

All plain JSON and Markdown, so they can be committed with the manuscript and diffed.

dsh-refkeeper README · Limits：- It is not a replacement for Zotero. Zotero handles a personal library across years (PDFs, styles, sync). This plugin covers the citations in one manuscript, as they appear in a conversation.
- It does not read PDFs. Everything comes from the conversation text and the registries.
- Exports are limited to the session workspace by the host's sandbox.
- A capture spends one model call (60 second cap) and annotates at most 12 entries.
- Registry metadata for Chinese journals is sparse; see above.

dsh-refkeeper README · Data and privacy：- Requests leave the machine only for verification: the identifier or title is sent to Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv and DataCite.
- Annotations use the model already configured in the session; the plugin holds no API key of its own.
- No telemetry. The library is a local file.

dsh-refkeeper README · Development：```sh
npm ci
npm test          # vitest
npm run typecheck
npm run build     # tsdown for the host bundle, then the client bundle

`tsdown` clears `lib/`, so run the client bundle afterwards. Node 22 or newer.
